props.title: Better Days
props.initialSlug: Chinese drama addressing bullying and social pressure

sections.content: **Better Days** (2019) marked a breakthrough moment in Chinese youth cinema, tackling school bullying with unflinching intensity. Director Derek Tsang crafts a haunting portrait of academic pressure and teenage cruelty that echoes the raw emotional power of Thirteen (2003) and **All About Lily Chou-Chou** (2001). The film's exploration of systemic violence through the lens of college entrance exams connects to other Asian academic pressure films like A Silent Voice (2016) and Bad Genius (2017), but takes a darker, more visceral approach.

sections.content: The cinematography in **Better Days** employs a distinctive visual language reminiscent of Wong Kar-wai's urban alienation, particularly in Chungking Express (1994). Zhou Dongyu's vulnerable performance as Chen Nian draws parallels to other powerful youth performances like Wei Zhao in **So Young** (2013). The film's unflinching look at institutional failure echoes social critique elements found in An Elephant Sitting Still (2018) and **Last Train Home** (2009).

The romance subplot between Chen Nian and Jackson Yee's character Xiao Bei creates a tender counterpoint to the violence, similar to the way **Let the Right One In** (2008) uses young love to offset darkness. This combination of gentle intimacy and brutal reality creates a tonal complexity that elevates the film beyond typical teen dramas or social issue films. sections.content: **Better Days** helped usher in a new wave of socially conscious Chinese youth films, including **Soul Mate** (2016) and **Us and Them** (2018). Its commercial success while maintaining artistic integrity opened doors for other directors tackling difficult subjects through a youth lens, similar to how **Farewell My Concubine** (1993) created space for historical critique through personal stories.

The film's international recognition, including an Oscar nomination, positions it alongside other breakthrough Asian social dramas like **Shoplifters** (2018) and **Burning** (2018). Its influence can be seen in subsequent works addressing academic pressure and youth violence, including **House of Hummingbird** (2018) and **Girl$ ** (2010).
